precincts.name: Arrivals
precincts.role: Hall of Arrivals, arrival hangar, shuttle pads
precincts.intro: 8,202 × 4,341 ft (2.5 × 1.32 km). Where every arrival steps aboard.

buildings.name: Hall of Arrivals
buildings.purpose: The front door of the Invicta. Every shuttle passenger steps off into this great hall, is greeted, and is sent on to customs, the terminals or the Keelway. It is the landmark of Deck 5 and the first room most visitors ever see aboard.

buildings.name: Arrival hangar
buildings.notes: Canon, bow side of the Hall
buildings.purpose: A single covered bay on the bow side of the Hall where an arriving shuttle can be parked indoors, unloaded under cover and turned around without blocking the open gates.

buildings.name: Shuttle gates G1–G16
buildings.notes: G1–G5 bow side, G6–G16 stern side, each with its own dock door
buildings.structure: Steel portal frame per bay, one full-width door to the apron (matches the canon Arrival hangar, 80 × 60 × 15 m).
buildings.look: Gunmetal sheds with full-width bay doors and a light strip over each door. Port of Arrivals style: graphite and gunmetal metal cladding, white exterior light lines.
buildings.entrances: One full-width craft door per bay on the apron side; a staff door at the back.
buildings.services: Power, air and fuel points in every bay; fire suppression over each bay.
buildings.interior: Each bay is one open floor for a craft, with a small tool room and a staff door at the back.
buildings.capacity: 16 bays, one craft each
buildings.purpose: Sixteen gates along the hull where passenger shuttles dock. Each gate has its own door to the apron, so a shuttle can open up, let its passengers walk into the concourse and leave again while the next one waits.

buildings.name: Gate Concourse
buildings.notes: Behind the gates, links every gate to the Hall
buildings.purpose: A covered walkway running behind all sixteen gates. Passengers walk along it from their shuttle to the Hall of Arrivals, and staff use it to move between gates without crossing the aprons.

buildings.name: Apron yards
buildings.size_text: between the concourse and Gate Road
buildings.purpose: The working ground behind the gates where baggage carts, fuel trucks and ground crews serve each docked shuttle. Passengers never come here; it keeps the turnaround work off the concourse.

buildings.name: Gate Road
buildings.notes: Service road behind the Hall, full length of the precinct
buildings.purpose: The service road behind the Hall of Arrivals. Trucks, fuel carts and baggage trains use it to reach every gate and apron along the precinct without mixing with passenger traffic.

buildings.name: Arrivals Forecourt
buildings.notes: Plaza at the Hall's main entrance
buildings.purpose: The open plaza at the Hall's main doors. Arriving travellers come out here to meet friends, find their pod or taxi, and get their first look down the boulevard into the port.

buildings.name: Pickup lanes
buildings.notes: Pods and taxis, either side of the boulevard
buildings.purpose: Drop-off and pickup lanes for pods and taxis on both sides of the boulevard, so travellers leaving the Hall can be collected straight from the forecourt.

buildings.name: Arrivals Boulevard
buildings.notes: From the forecourt inland along F43 to P5 Terminals
buildings.purpose: The main street out of the arrivals precinct. It carries travellers from the forecourt inland along F43 to the Terminals, with walkways, trees and the pickup lanes along it.

buildings.name: Streets
buildings.size_text: F42, F44, F45 Streets, 98 ft (30 m)
buildings.purpose: The cross streets that link Gate Road to Dock Road, giving staff, service vehicles and emergency crews short routes through the precinct blocks.

buildings.name: Dock Road
buildings.notes: Precinct edge (lanes C/D), arterial to Bow and Stern Docks
buildings.purpose: The arterial road along the precinct edge, linking Arrivals to the Bow and Stern Docks. Freight, service vehicles and through traffic use it so they stay out of the passenger streets.

buildings.name: Port Health
buildings.structure: Concrete frame on a 9 m grid; the quarantine wing is sealed with its own air supply.
buildings.look: A clean white building of frosted glass and pale ceramic panels in a U around a healing garden, with a soft green light line marking the screening entrance.
buildings.entrances: Arrivals reach the screening hall from the gates side; ambulances use the bay at the back.
buildings.capacity: About 3,000 arrivals screened an hour; 60 ward beds and 46 quarantine suites.
buildings.services: Separate air for the quarantine wing, 4 stair and lift cores, decontamination suite.
buildings.interior: A screening hall with booths and scan gates along the gates side; a clinic wing with treatment rooms, imaging, lab and wards; a sealed quarantine wing with negative-pressure rooms and quarantine suites; a healing garden between them.
buildings.purpose: The port's health checkpoint. Arrivals who need it are screened here for disease and contamination, and anyone who must be kept apart is cared for in its quarantine ward before entering the ship.

buildings.name: Arrivals Fire Station
buildings.structure: Steel appliance hall, 9 m (30 ft) clear; three-storey concrete crew block.
buildings.look: A compact station of red-framed glass bay doors under a dark crew block with a single lit red stripe, facing the arrival gates.
buildings.entrances: Six appliance doors toward the gates; crew door from the drill yard.
buildings.capacity: 6 appliances; 18 crew on watch.
buildings.services: Foam refill, medical store, 2 stair cores.
buildings.interior: A six-bay appliance hall, a crew block with watch room and medical store, bunk rooms and mess, and offices on top, and a drill yard behind.
buildings.purpose: The fire and rescue station for the shuttle gates. Its crash crews stand ready for a fire, fuel spill or hard landing on the aprons and reach any gate within minutes.

buildings.name: Baggage Hall
buildings.structure: Steel roof on a 24 m grid over a column-free reclaim hall, 9 m (30 ft) clear; baggage tunnel in concrete below.
buildings.look: A bright hall under a white folded roof with long rooflights, glass walls on the forecourt side so arrivals can see their way out.
buildings.entrances: Arrivals come in from the Hall of Arrivals; exits through customs channels to the forecourt.
buildings.capacity: 6 reclaim belts; about 4,000 arrivals an hour.
buildings.services: Bags arrive by tunnel from Baggage Logistics in P4; 2 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: Six reclaim belts in one hall, fed from a bag tunnel below, with lost luggage, oversize bags and the customs red and green channels on the way out.
buildings.purpose: Where arrivals collect their luggage from the reclaim belts. It also runs the lost-luggage desk and hands bags on to the baggage system in the Freight precinct.

buildings.name: Visitor Centre
buildings.structure: Timber and steel roof on tree-like columns over a two-storey glass pavilion.
buildings.look: A welcoming glass pavilion under a wide wave-shaped timber roof, with a giant lit model of the Invicta inside visible from the forecourt.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance from the Arrivals Forecourt; garden doors on the forecourt side.
buildings.capacity: About 2,000 visitors at a time; 120 guides and staff.
buildings.services: 2 stair and lift cores, baggage drop, multilingual guides.
buildings.interior: Welcome desks, a ship map wall with a large model of the Invicta, travel shop and café on the ground floor; the Invicta exhibition, cinema and group rooms upstairs; a roof viewing deck.
buildings.purpose: The welcome desk for newcomers. Guides hand out maps, explain how the ship works, book tours and help visitors find where they are staying.

buildings.name: Arrivals Police Post
buildings.structure: Reinforced concrete frame with a hardened ground floor.
buildings.look: A small two-storey block in charcoal panels with a blue light band, tucked beside the gate road.
buildings.entrances: Public entrance at the front; vehicle gate at the back.
buildings.capacity: About 80 officers across three shifts.
buildings.services: 1 stair core, holding rooms, CCTV link to the Hall of Arrivals.
buildings.interior: Front desk, interview and holding rooms below, open office and briefing room above, and a garage wing round a secure yard.
buildings.purpose: The police and security post for the arrivals area. Officers here patrol the Hall and gates, handle lost people and trouble on arrival, and work with customs and port health.

buildings.name: Gate Operations
buildings.structure: Concrete frame with a steel and glass top floor; steel equipment hall behind.
buildings.look: A four-storey block of dark glass and gunmetal fins topped by a glass gate control floor that looks out over all sixteen shuttle gates, with a ground equipment hall behind.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance on the gates side; equipment hall doors to the yard.
buildings.capacity: About 700 staff across shifts; the control floor runs all 16 gates.
buildings.services: 2 stair and lift cores, backup power and comms.
buildings.interior: Ground floor: gate crew room, ramp equipment store, lockers and canteen. Levels 2 and 3: dispatch, training and offices. Level 4: the gate control room overlooking every gate. A four-bay ground equipment hall behind.
buildings.purpose: The control room for the sixteen shuttle gates. Staff here assign gates, schedule docking and departures, and dispatch the ground crews that serve each shuttle.

buildings.name: Staff Centre
buildings.structure: Concrete frame on an 8 m grid.
buildings.look: A three-sided staff building in warm grey metal and timber around a green garden, with big canteen windows facing it.
buildings.entrances: Staff entrance from the gate road; garden doors from the canteen.
buildings.capacity: Canteen seats 1,200; lockers for about 4,000 staff.
buildings.services: 2 stair and lift cores, 24-hour canteen.
buildings.interior: A front block with staff entrance, canteen and shop, and training, HR and welfare rooms upstairs; a locker wing and a rest wing with quiet room, prayer rooms, nap pods, gym and rest rooms; a staff garden in the middle.
buildings.purpose: The staff building for everyone who works in Arrivals: canteen, locker rooms and rest areas where gate, baggage and hall staff take their breaks and change shifts.

buildings.name: Crew Lodge
buildings.floors: Level −1 (below deck); Levels 1–3 in the main block, 79 ft (24 m); Levels 4–5 in the towers, to 125 ft (38 m)
buildings.capacity: 640 cabins (480 standard + 160 tower quarters), rated for 1,280 crew on rotating shifts
buildings.entrances: Prow Entrance; Starboard Service Access; no entrance on the stern side
buildings.structure: Steel frame on a 39 × 39 ft (12 × 12 m) grid, composite slabs, bearing on the deck plating. Main block (Levels 1–3) covers the full footprint at 26 ft (8 m) floor to floor. Four corner towers, each about 262 × 197 ft (80 × 60 m), add Levels 4–5 at 23 ft (7 m) to 125 ft (38 m). Stair and lift cores about every 328 ft (100 m), plus one core per tower from Level −1 to the roof. Level −1, the Crew Undercroft, is 20 ft (6 m) deep in the top of the 197 ft (60 m) service layer, clear of the gravity plates, with plant, laundry, stores and a crew-only tunnel door into the service-layer tunnels. Sits wholly within one pressure zone (F45–F46).
buildings.look: Graphite and gunmetal metal cladding, titanium composite, smart glass and silver structural accents; ice-blue and white exterior lighting; warm amber and soft-white interiors; polished stone composite in public areas, warm wood-tone and acoustic finishes in residential areas.
buildings.services: 24-hour reception and check-in, luggage handling, dining hall, cafeteria, coffee bar and late-night meals, communal kitchen, fitness centre and walking track, movie theatre, gaming and entertainment rooms, medical station, wellness and recovery rooms, industrial laundry and linen, housekeeping, maintenance workshop, mechanical plant, water treatment and building automation.
buildings.interior: Level −1: laundry, plant, electrical, water, workshop, stores, receiving and the secure crew tunnel. Level 1: Prow Entrance, reception, luggage, operations, security, medical, dining hall and kitchen, lounges, shop, central atrium and courtyard garden. Level 2: four cabin wings (240 cabins), fitness centre, theatre, gaming, wellness, communal kitchen, study rooms. Level 3: four cabin wings (240 cabins) and quiet lounges. Levels 4–5: four towers, each with 20 quarters per level (160 in total) and a lounge.
buildings.purpose: Rooms for shuttle crews between flights. Pilots and cabin crew sleep and rest here close to the gates instead of travelling to homes elsewhere in the ship.

buildings.name: Arrivals Utility Plant
buildings.structure: Concrete plant house; steel chiller enclosures.
buildings.look: A plain graphite plant house with three louvred chiller boxes beside it.
buildings.entrances: Service doors on the gate road side.
buildings.capacity: Power, water and cooling for P2; about 20 staff per shift.
buildings.services: Six transformers, water pumps, air handling, three chillers.
buildings.interior: A plant house with transformer bays, switch room and water pumps below, air handling above, and three chillers alongside.
buildings.purpose: The local utility plant for the arrivals precinct. It steps down power, moves fresh air and supplies water and cooling to the Hall, the gates and the buildings around them.

buildings.name: Service Shaft 1
buildings.notes: Access to the 60 m service layer · bow shaft, beside Street 1
buildings.structure: Concrete shaft walls down to the 60 m (197 ft) service layer; steel head house.
buildings.look: A narrow graphite head house with yellow-striped lift doors beside Street 1.
buildings.entrances: Vehicle queue on the starboard side; staff door into the control house.
buildings.capacity: One vehicle lift and one goods lift.
buildings.services: Lift machinery and shaft ventilation.
buildings.interior: A control house and a shaft hall with a vehicle lift and a goods lift down to the service layer.
buildings.purpose: A lift shaft down to the service layer under the deck at the bow end of the precinct. Maintenance crews and goods move up and down here without using the streets.

buildings.name: Service Shaft 2
buildings.notes: Access to the 60 m service layer · stern shaft
buildings.structure: Concrete shaft walls down to the 60 m (197 ft) service layer; steel head house with crane rails.
buildings.look: A tall graphite head house with big louvres and yellow-striped lift doors.
buildings.entrances: Vehicle ramp on the starboard side; staff door into the control house.
buildings.capacity: Two vehicle lifts and one goods lift.
buildings.services: Lift machinery, shaft ventilation, emergency stair.
buildings.interior: A control house with shaft control and fans, and a shaft hall with two vehicle lifts and a goods lift down to the service layer.
buildings.purpose: The stern-end shaft to the service layer under the precinct. Its vehicle and goods lifts let crews bring heavy equipment up to Arrivals and take waste down.

buildings.name: Bow Garden / Stern Garden
buildings.purpose: Two parks either side of the boulevard where travellers can sit in green space after their flight, wait for friends, or take a first walk before heading on.

precincts.name: Terminals
precincts.role: Departure and arrival halls, check-in, customs, security
precincts.intro: 14,764 × 4,921 ft (4.5 × 1.5 km). Departures and arrivals for the whole ship. Arrivals Boulevard runs through the middle; people movers link both terminals to the P2 gate concourse.

buildings.name: Transfer Hall
buildings.notes: travellers from other decks · shuttle bookings
buildings.structure: A steel lattice dome, 32 m (105 ft) high and 300 m (984 ft) across, on a concrete ring; concrete arms around it.
buildings.look: A cross-shaped terminal with a great shallow dome of triangulated glass and titanium at its centre, glowing amber at night like a beacon for travellers from other decks; the four arms are low and dark.
buildings.entrances: Kerb entrance from the Terminal Road; link from the arrival gates on the port side; deck lifts below the dome.
buildings.capacity: About 12,000 transfer travellers an hour.
buildings.services: Deck lifts under the dome, baggage transfer belts, 6 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: A domed great hall at the crossing of four arms: deck transfer desks, ticketing and lounges in the bow arm, shuttle booking and baggage transfer in the stern arm, the link to the gates on the port side and the kerb hall on the landside. Food court and business lounges upstairs; deck lifts and baggage belts below.
buildings.purpose: The hall for travellers changing between the shuttles and the rest of the ship. People arriving from other decks or going on to another shuttle check bookings and wait here.

buildings.name: Arrivals Terminal
buildings.notes: passport and customs control · baggage claim
buildings.structure: Steel roof on tree columns on a 36 m grid, 15 m (49 ft) clear, over a concrete baggage level.
buildings.look: A long, calm terminal under a rippling white roof held up by branching steel columns; glass walls along the kerb, warm timber ceilings and a lit wall of welcome messages in many languages.
buildings.entrances: Arrivals walk in from the gates on the port side; exits to the arrivals kerb on the Terminal Road.
buildings.capacity: About 6,000 arrivals an hour; 8 reclaim belts.
buildings.services: Baggage by tunnel from P4, 3 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: Three halls in sequence from the gates to the kerb: immigration (passport control, automated gates, secondary checks), reclaim and customs, and the arrivals meeting hall with welcome desks, pod and taxi desks, shops and cafés, and an arrivals lounge upstairs.
buildings.purpose: Where arriving passengers go through passport and customs control and collect checked baggage before entering the ship proper.

buildings.name: Departures Terminal
buildings.structure: Long-span steel wave roof, 22 m (72 ft) high over the check-in hall, on a concrete departures deck.
buildings.look: A soaring wave-shaped roof that rises over the check-in hall and dips toward the gates, clad in titanium with a sawtooth of rooflights; the kerb front is a 760 m (2,493 ft) glass wall.
buildings.entrances: Departures kerb on the Terminal Road; travellers leave toward the gates on the port side.
buildings.capacity: About 6,000 departing travellers an hour; 16 security lanes.
buildings.services: Baggage tunnel to P4, 5 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: From the kerb to the gates: a check-in hall with six check-in islands and bag drop, a security and passport exit hall, and the departure lounges with gate lounges, a departures street of duty-free shops and restaurants, and first-class, business and quiet lounges on the top level.
buildings.purpose: Where travellers leaving the Invicta check in, pass security screening and wait in lounges until their shuttle is called at the gates.

buildings.name: Cargo Customs
buildings.structure: Steel portal frames, 10 m (33 ft) clear, over the inspection lanes; shielded concrete scanner hall.
buildings.look: A long low inspection shed in customs-blue metal with numbered lanes lit above each door, a heavy concrete scanner hall at one end and a three-storey office block along the landside.
buildings.entrances: Trucks queue from the Dock Road side and leave released into the cargo yard; brokers and staff enter the office block from the Terminal Road.
buildings.capacity: 8 inspection lanes and 2 scanners; about 400 trucks a day; 500 staff.
buildings.services: Container X-ray, radiation portals, detector dogs, 3 stair cores.
buildings.interior: A truck queue, an eight-lane inspection shed, a scanner hall with a container X-ray and a radiation portal, and an office block with declarations hall, brokers' counters, sample lab, seized goods vault and customs offices.
buildings.purpose: The customs post for cargo. Incoming freight is inspected, scanned and held in bond here until its declarations are cleared and duties are paid.

buildings.name: Terminals Private Flights Lounge
buildings.structure: Steel frame with stone cladding; timber roof terrace.
buildings.look: A long low house of honey-coloured stone and bronze-framed glass between a garden court and a car court, with a roof bar under a light canopy.
buildings.entrances: Valet kerb on the Terminal Road; private transfer to the Stern Docks private berths.
buildings.capacity: About 200 guests at a time.
buildings.services: Private customs, valet, 2 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: Private check-in and customs, main lounge and dining room on the ground floor, private suites and spa above, a roof bar on top, with a garden court on one side and a car court on the other.
buildings.purpose: A private lounge for passengers of private and charter flights docking at the Stern Docks, with its own quiet check-in away from the main terminals.

buildings.name: Travel Office
buildings.structure: Concrete frame with a glass arcade roof.
buildings.look: A three-storey block of cream panels with a glass-roofed arcade running through it and big departure boards visible from the street.
buildings.entrances: Arcade entrances from the Terminal Road and from the garden.
buildings.capacity: About 3,000 visitors a day; 400 staff including the call centre.
buildings.services: 2 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: A ticket hall with ticket counters, travel information and kiosks along an arcade, with booking offices and a call centre on the upper floors.
buildings.purpose: The ticket and information office for travel to, from and around the ship. Travellers book shuttles, change bookings and ask for help here.

buildings.name: Terminals Pod Depot
buildings.structure: Post-tensioned concrete parking decks.
buildings.look: A four-deck pod garage with angled gunmetal screens and green charging lights.
buildings.entrances: Pod lanes on the Concourse Road side.
buildings.capacity: About 2,000 pods.
buildings.services: Charging at every space, pod wash, battery swap.
buildings.interior: Four decks of pod parking and charging and a dispatch strip with pod wash and battery swap.
buildings.purpose: The depot where the terminals' ground pods and taxis are parked, charged and dispatched to pick up travellers.

buildings.name: Customs & Border Hq
buildings.structure: Concrete frame with blast-resistant facades on a 9 m grid.
buildings.look: An H-shaped six-storey headquarters in dark granite-coloured panels with deep narrow windows, the link block glowing behind a glass front with the border service crest.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance from the front court on the Concourse Road side; secure vehicle access through the secure court.
buildings.capacity: About 2,500 staff.
buildings.services: 5 stair and lift cores, joint operations centre, custody suite, backup power.
buildings.interior: Two six-storey blocks joined by a link: border police station and custody suite in the bow block, customs intelligence and labs in the stern block, the entrance hall and public enquiries in the link, with the joint operations centre above it. Offices on the upper floors; a front court and a secure court.
buildings.purpose: Headquarters for customs and border control in the port and the main police station for the terminals. Officers who staff passport desks and cargo inspection are based here.

buildings.name: Terminal Plaza
buildings.purpose: The open square in front of the terminals where travellers meet, wait between connections and find their way to the halls around it.

buildings.name: Licensing & Permits
buildings.structure: Concrete frame round a courtyard; a long-span timber roof over the public service hall.
buildings.look: A four-storey ring of pale terracotta-coloured panels around a courtyard, fronted by a single-storey public hall with a sweeping timber roof and a clear queue display wall.
buildings.entrances: Public entrance from the plaza on the Concourse Road side.
buildings.capacity: About 5,000 visitors a day; 900 staff.
buildings.services: 4 stair and lift cores, online queue system.
buildings.interior: A public service hall with queue area, 30 service counters, interview rooms and cashier; behind it a ring of offices round a courtyard, with the flight, cargo and travel permit offices on the ground floor and licensing offices above.
buildings.purpose: The permits office. Pilots, shipping firms and travellers come here to apply for flight licences, cargo permits and travel papers.

buildings.name: Terminal Admin
buildings.structure: Concrete core and steel frame tower on a two-storey podium.
buildings.look: A slim 12-storey tower of pale glass with vertical bronze ribs rising from a stone podium, its top floor ringed with a gold light band; the port authority seal over the entrance.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance from the garden side; podium entrance from the Terminal Road.
buildings.capacity: About 1,300 port authority staff.
buildings.services: 4 stair and lift cores, conference hall.
buildings.interior: A podium with the port authority reception, an exhibition hall and a conference hall, and a ten-storey office tower above with the board room and executive offices on top.
buildings.purpose: The port authority's offices. The people who run the Port of Arrivals, from planning to finance and staffing, work here.

buildings.name: Terminals Utility Plant
buildings.structure: Concrete plant house; steel chiller hall.
buildings.look: A plain graphite plant house with louvred walls.
buildings.entrances: Service doors on the Terminal Road side.
buildings.capacity: Power, cooling and water for P5; about 25 staff per shift.
buildings.services: Six transformers, air handling, chillers and water pumps.
buildings.interior: A plant house with transformer bays, switch and control rooms and air handling, and a chiller and pump hall.
buildings.purpose: The terminals' own utility plant, supplying power, fresh air, cooling and water to the passenger halls around it.

buildings.name: Terminals Service Shaft
buildings.structure: Concrete shaft walls down to the 60 m (197 ft) service layer; steel head house.
buildings.look: A narrow graphite head house with yellow-striped lift doors.
buildings.entrances: Vehicle queue on the Concourse Road side; staff door into the control house.
buildings.capacity: A vehicle lift, a goods lift and a baggage lift.
buildings.services: Lift machinery and shaft ventilation.
buildings.interior: A control house and a shaft hall with vehicle, goods and baggage lifts down to the service layer.
buildings.purpose: A service shaft from the terminals to the layer under the deck, with a lift for vehicles, one for goods and one dedicated to moving baggage.

buildings.name: Medical Centre
buildings.structure: Concrete frame on a 9 m grid with a four-storey ward slab on the clinic podium.
buildings.look: A white clinic podium with a slim ward slab above it, its windows shaded by pale vertical fins; a red-and-white lit emergency canopy facing the ambulance court.
buildings.entrances: Emergency entrance from the ambulance court; outpatient entrance from the Terminal Road.
buildings.capacity: About 120 beds and 4 operating theatres.
buildings.services: 4 stair and lift cores, bed lifts, medical gases, backup power.
buildings.interior: A two-storey clinic podium with the emergency department, first aid, imaging and pharmacy below and operating theatres, outpatient clinics and lab above; a four-storey ward slab on top; stores, plant and morgue below deck; an ambulance court and a healing garden.
buildings.purpose: The main medical centre for the terminals, with a clinic, beds and operating theatres for travellers and port staff who fall ill or are hurt.

precincts.name: Concourse
precincts.role: Transit lounges, travellers' hotels, shops, greeters
precincts.intro: 14,764 × 4,921 ft (4.5 × 1.5 km). Where travellers wait, eat and sleep. The boulevard becomes the 394 ft (120 m) tree-lined Concourse Promenade. Hotel room counts are placeholders.

buildings.name: Greeters' Hall
buildings.structure: Steel space-frame roof, 21 m (69 ft) high, on eight tree columns; concrete service wing.
buildings.look: A tall, airy hall under a glowing white space-frame roof with big arrival boards, glass on all sides; meeting crowds are visible from the street.
buildings.entrances: Arrivals come in under the canopy from the terminals; doors to the waiting garden on Hotel Row.
buildings.capacity: About 5,000 people waiting at a time.
buildings.services: Arrival boards linked to every gate, 2 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: One great greeting hall where people meet arriving travellers, with welcome desks, gift shops, cafés, lost and found and a family room in the service wing and a gallery lounge above, and a waiting garden behind.
buildings.purpose: The meeting place where friends and family wait for arriving travellers, with welcome desks and a big arrivals board.

buildings.name: Shop Arcade
buildings.structure: Steel frame on a 10 m grid with glass barrel roofs over the two arcades.
buildings.look: Two three-storey shop bars with glass barrel roofs over their arcades, warm shopfront light spilling out, linked by bridges across an open middle court.
buildings.entrances: Arcade entrances at both ends, from the Concourse Road and from Hotel Row.
buildings.capacity: About 90 shops; about 8,000 visitors at a time.
buildings.services: 6 stair and lift cores, service lanes at the back of the shops.
buildings.interior: Two shop bars, each with its own glass-roofed arcade: duty-free, travel goods, pharmacy, grocery, books and banking on the ground floor, fashion and electronics above, restaurants, a food court and a cinema on top.
buildings.purpose: A covered shopping street for travellers selling travel goods, souvenirs and duty-free items between the terminals and the hotels.

buildings.name: Transit Lounges
buildings.structure: Concrete frame with stepped terraces, each floor set back over the one below.
buildings.look: A long building that steps back in three planted terraces toward the garden courts, with timber screens and soft lighting; quiet and calm after the terminals.
buildings.entrances: From the Concourse Road side and from the Concourse Promenade on the stern side.
buildings.capacity: About 6,000 travellers resting at a time; 360 sleep cabins.
buildings.services: 6 stair and lift cores, showers, sleep cabins by the hour.
buildings.interior: A long lounge building with the main transit lounge, showers, family lounge, prayer rooms and cafés on the ground floor, quiet and work lounges, sleep pods and a spa above, and a roof garden lounge; a pod hotel of sleep cabins behind it, and garden courts.
buildings.purpose: Rest areas for travellers between connections, with seating, sleep pods and showers so long waits are comfortable.

buildings.name: Market Hall
buildings.structure: Cast-steel arches spanning 320 m (1,050 ft) under a glass-and-timber vault, 21 m (69 ft) high.
buildings.look: A great vaulted market hall of arched steel ribs and timber panels with a long glass roof, flanked by two lines of small shops; busy, warm and noisy.
buildings.entrances: Open market squares at both ends; shop doors on both long sides; deliveries from Hotel Row.
buildings.capacity: About 300 stalls and 48 shops; about 10,000 visitors at a time.
buildings.services: 4 stair cores, cold rooms, waste and recycling yard.
buildings.interior: A vaulted market hall with fresh produce, bakers, butchers, spice, street food and flower stalls and a seating hall, two lines of shops with a cooking school and market offices above, open market squares at each end and a delivery yard.
buildings.purpose: The concourse's indoor market and food court, where travellers and port workers buy meals, groceries and everyday goods.

buildings.name: Restaurant Row
buildings.structure: Concrete frame with timber floors; restaurants open onto the terrace with folding glass walls.
buildings.look: Two long rows of restaurants facing each other across a terrace and a lit water channel, each with its own coloured awning and roof garden bar.
buildings.entrances: Every restaurant opens onto the waterside terrace; deliveries from the service lane.
buildings.capacity: About 60 restaurants and bars; about 9,000 diners at a time.
buildings.services: 6 stair and lift cores, grease and waste lines, kitchen extract.
buildings.interior: Two rows of restaurants with private dining and bars upstairs, a music venue, and roof terrace bars, facing a waterside terrace and channel.
buildings.purpose: A street of restaurants and cafés serving travellers, hotel guests and port staff.

buildings.name: Travellers' Clinic
buildings.structure: Concrete frame on a 9 m grid.
buildings.look: An L-shaped white clinic with green-tinted glass and a small healing garden in its corner.
buildings.entrances: Walk-in entrance from the Concourse Road side.
buildings.capacity: About 1,500 patients a day; 40 short-stay beds.
buildings.services: 3 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: A walk-in clinic with vaccination rooms, pharmacy, consulting rooms, a travel health lab and a short-stay ward, and a side wing with dental, eye, imaging and physio clinics round a garden.
buildings.purpose: A clinic for travellers staying in the concourse hotels, treating illness and minor injuries without a trip to the terminals' medical centre.

buildings.name: Concourse Police Post
buildings.structure: Reinforced concrete frame with a hardened ground floor.
buildings.look: A long two-storey charcoal block with a blue light band and a glass front desk facing the concourse.
buildings.entrances: Public entrance from the Concourse Road; vehicle yard behind.
buildings.capacity: About 120 officers across three shifts.
buildings.services: 2 stair cores, CCTV room covering the concourse.
buildings.interior: Front desk, interview and holding rooms, lost property and garage below; open office, CCTV room and briefing room above.
buildings.purpose: The police post for the hotels, shops and lounges of the concourse, keeping the busy public areas safe day and night.

buildings.name: Promenade Park
buildings.purpose: A large park running through the concourse where travellers walk, rest and stretch their legs between flights.

buildings.name: Pod Stop
buildings.purpose: The local pod stop serving the concourse's hotels and shops.

buildings.name: Grand Port Hotel
buildings.structure: Concrete core towers with flat slabs on a two-storey steel and stone podium.
buildings.look: The port's flagship: two slim 80 m (263 ft) towers of champagne-tinted glass with bronze fins rising from a long white stone podium, joined at the top by lit sky lounges; a grand entrance court with a fountain on Hotel Row.
buildings.entrances: Grand entrance court on Hotel Row; garden entrance on the Station Road side.
buildings.capacity: About 1,200 guest rooms (from the brief), in two towers of 17 guest floors.
buildings.services: 8 stair and lift cores, ballroom, spa and pool, sky bar.
buildings.interior: A two-storey podium with grand lobby, restaurants, bar, shops, ballroom, meeting rooms, spa and pool, and two guest towers of 17 floors each with a sky bar and sky restaurant on top; hotel gardens behind.
buildings.purpose: The port's flagship hotel, where important visitors, officials and wealthy travellers stay when they arrive aboard.

buildings.name: Harbour Hotel
buildings.structure: Concrete flat-slab wings, eight storeys on the long sides and six on the short sides.
buildings.look: A mid-range courtyard hotel in white render and blue-grey metal balconies, wrapped around a big garden with a pool; striped awnings on the ground-floor restaurant.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance from the drop-off on Hotel Row.
buildings.capacity: About 900 guest rooms (from the brief).
buildings.services: 10 stair and lift cores, pool, gym, meeting rooms.
buildings.interior: Four wings round a garden and pool: lobby, restaurant and bar at the front, meeting rooms and gym at the back, guest rooms on every floor above.
buildings.purpose: A mid-range hotel for ordinary travellers staying a few nights near the port.

buildings.name: Crew Hotel
buildings.structure: Concrete flat-slab slabs, ten storeys, joined by a two-storey link.
buildings.look: Two plain, neat ten-storey slabs in pale grey with coloured window panels for each airline crew floor, joined by a glass link.
buildings.entrances: Drop-off and entrance on Hotel Row.
buildings.capacity: About 900 crew rooms.
buildings.services: 5 stair and lift cores, 24-hour canteen, shuttle bus to the gates.
buildings.interior: Two crew room slabs with reception, canteen, laundry, lounge and gym on the ground floors, joined by a link with a shuttle bus lounge.
buildings.purpose: A large hotel for shuttle and ship crews on layover, close to the gates and docks.

buildings.name: Port Hostel
buildings.structure: Modular steel-frame capsule floors on a concrete ground floor.
buildings.look: A bright, cheerful six-storey block in orange and white panels with a lit roof deck and a courtyard full of tables.
buildings.entrances: Entrance from Hotel Row.
buildings.capacity: About 3,800 capsule beds.
buildings.services: 2 stair and lift cores, shared kitchen and bathrooms.
buildings.interior: Reception, common kitchen and common room below, four floors of capsule rooms, and a roof deck; a courtyard and a bike and pod stand behind.
buildings.purpose: A budget hostel with capsule rooms for travellers on a tight budget or a short stopover.

buildings.name: Concourse Utility Plant
buildings.structure: Concrete plant floors with blast walls; steel roof.
buildings.look: Plain graphite sheds with tall louvres and a round-topped water tank.
buildings.entrances: Service doors on Hotel Row.
buildings.capacity: Power, cooling and water for P6; about 25 staff per shift.
buildings.services: Six transformers, chillers, air handling, water pumps.
buildings.interior: A substation, a plant hall with chillers, air handling and water pumps, and a water tank.
buildings.purpose: The utility plant for the concourse, supplying power, air, water and cooling to its hotels, shops and halls.

buildings.name: Concourse Service Shaft
buildings.structure: Concrete shaft walls down to the 60 m (197 ft) service layer; steel head house.
buildings.look: A tall graphite head house with yellow-striped lift doors.
buildings.entrances: Vehicle queue on the Station Road side; staff door into the control house.
buildings.capacity: A vehicle lift, a goods lift and a hotel supplies lift.
buildings.services: Lift machinery and shaft ventilation.
buildings.interior: A control house and a shaft hall with three lifts down to the service layer.
buildings.purpose: The concourse's shaft down to the service layer, used to bring in supplies for the hotels and shops and take waste away.

precincts.name: Station
precincts.role: Keelway Port station (F46), interchange, deck-transfer lifts
precincts.intro: 14,764 × 5,741 ft (4.5 × 1.75 km). The interchange. Keelway Port station (canon stop at F46) with its platforms, Keelway Square where the boulevard ends, pods and taxis. Deck-transfer lifts approved as canon by Jordan.

buildings.name: Porters' Hall
buildings.structure: Concrete frame with a steel automated luggage store.
buildings.look: A three-storey brick-red building with a wide glazed trolley street through the middle and a windowless luggage tower behind, its sides lit with a moving light strip.
buildings.entrances: Trolley street entrances from the Station Road and from the cart yard.
buildings.capacity: About 40,000 bags stored; 600 porters.
buildings.services: Automated luggage store, 2 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: Porter booking desks, luggage storage, lost and found and the trolley store along a trolley street, porters' lockers, canteen and offices upstairs, an automated luggage tower behind, and a cart yard and drop-off.
buildings.purpose: The porters' base at the Keelway station. Porters carry luggage for travellers between the station and the port, and the lost and found office is here.

buildings.name: Station Shops
buildings.structure: Steel frame on a 10 m grid with a rooflit shop street.
buildings.look: A square two-storey shop hall with a long rooflight over its shop street and a bright supermarket front onto the Station Road.
buildings.entrances: Shop street entrances from the Station Road and the shop square.
buildings.capacity: About 30 shops and a supermarket; 4,000 shoppers at a time.
buildings.services: 2 stair and lift cores, service yard.
buildings.interior: A shop street with a supermarket, pharmacy, bakery, newsagent and small shops below, and a food court, post office, bank and shops above; a service yard and a shop square.
buildings.purpose: Everyday shops at the station, such as a grocery and a pharmacy, for travellers and commuters passing through.

buildings.name: Interchange Hall
buildings.structure: Steel trusses on a 60 m (197 ft) grid over twelve drive-through bays; concrete concourse.
buildings.look: A long concourse under a sawtooth roof of white steel and glass, opening onto twelve drive-through bays where pods and buses pull up under lit bay numbers.
buildings.entrances: Concourse doors from the Station Road; vehicles enter the bays from the Interchange Road.
buildings.capacity: 12 bays; about 15,000 passengers an hour.
buildings.services: 4 stair and lift cores, real-time departure boards.
buildings.interior: A concourse with ticket hall, travel information, waiting rooms and cafés, a departure board hall and transport control upstairs, and twelve drive-through pod and bus bays behind it, then the taxi rank.
buildings.purpose: The hall where travellers change from the Keelway to pods, taxis and other ground transport across the port.

buildings.name: Station Clinic
buildings.structure: Concrete frame on a 9 m grid.
buildings.look: A low white clinic with a green cross lit over the door and a garden behind.
buildings.entrances: Walk-in entrance from the Station Road; ambulance bay behind.
buildings.capacity: About 800 patients a day.
buildings.services: 2 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: Walk-in clinic, first aid, pharmacy and waiting room below, consulting rooms above, a garden and an ambulance bay.
buildings.purpose: A clinic at the station for travellers and commuters who are taken ill or hurt on their journey.

buildings.name: Station Offices
buildings.structure: Steel frame with concrete cores.
buildings.look: A six-storey L of graphite glass with a glass-walled transit control room on level 2 showing the live Keelway map.
buildings.entrances: Entrance from the Station Road.
buildings.capacity: About 900 staff.
buildings.services: 3 stair and lift cores, backup power and comms.
buildings.interior: An L-shaped office with the entrance hall and staff room below, the Keelway transit control room on level 2, and transit offices above.
buildings.purpose: The station's offices and transit control room, which run the Keelway Port station, its platforms and lifts.

buildings.name: Deck-Transfer Lifts
buildings.purpose: Large lifts that carry people and goods between Deck 5 and the other decks of the ship.

buildings.name: Station Pod Depot
buildings.structure: Post-tensioned concrete parking decks.
buildings.look: A three-deck pod garage with perforated gunmetal screens and green charging lights.
buildings.entrances: Pod lanes on the Interchange Road side.
buildings.capacity: About 1,200 pods.
buildings.services: Charging at every space, pod wash, battery swap.
buildings.interior: Three decks of pod parking and charging and a dispatch strip.
buildings.purpose: The depot where the station's ground pods are parked, charged and sent out to waiting travellers.

buildings.name: Pod & Taxi Rank
buildings.purpose: The rank where pods and taxis queue to pick up travellers leaving the station.

buildings.name: Station Utility Plant
buildings.structure: Concrete plant floors with blast walls; steel roof.
buildings.look: Plain graphite sheds with tall louvres and a heavy cable gallery running to the Keelway.
buildings.entrances: Service yard on the Keelway side.
buildings.capacity: Power for P7 and Keelway traction power; about 30 staff per shift.
buildings.services: Eight transformers, traction power, chillers, air handling, water pumps.
buildings.interior: A substation with transformer bays and a Keelway traction power room, and a plant hall with chillers, air handling and water pumps.
buildings.purpose: The station's utility plant, supplying power, fresh air and cooling to the platforms and halls.

buildings.name: Station Service Shaft
buildings.structure: Concrete shaft walls down to the 60 m (197 ft) service layer; steel head house.
buildings.look: A wide graphite head house with yellow-striped lift doors.
buildings.entrances: Vehicle queue on the Keelway side; staff door into the control house.
buildings.capacity: Two vehicle lifts and a goods lift.
buildings.services: Lift machinery and shaft ventilation.
buildings.interior: A control house and a shaft hall with two vehicle lifts and a goods lift down to the service layer.
buildings.purpose: The station's shaft to the service layer, used by maintenance crews and for deliveries.

buildings.name: Keelway Square
buildings.purpose: The open square outside Keelway Port station where travellers gather, meet and set off into the port.

buildings.name: Station Walk
buildings.purpose: A covered moving walkway linking the station to the port's terminals and concourse.

buildings.name: Keelway Port Station
buildings.notes: platforms on the Keelway · centred on F46
buildings.structure: A steel arched train shed, 26 m (85 ft) high and 420 m (1,378 ft) deep, over the Keelway platforms; concrete concourse.
buildings.look: The port's railway cathedral: a long arched train shed of steel ribs and glass over the Keelway platforms, fronted by a broad glass concourse with a lit clock and the Keelway sign over the forecourt.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance from the station forecourt on the Interchange Road; platforms open to the Keelway on the starboard side.
buildings.capacity: 12 platforms; about 40,000 passengers an hour.
buildings.services: 6 stair, lift and escalator cores; platform screen doors; station control.
buildings.interior: A forecourt, a two-level concourse with ticket hall, gate lines, waiting hall, shops, cafés, food hall and first-class lounge, and the train shed with twelve platforms, a freight through-line and a maintenance siding; platform access halls below.
buildings.purpose: The Port of Arrivals stop on the Keelway, the ship's main rail line. Trains from every part of the deck stop at its platforms on F46.

precincts.name: Bow Docks
precincts.role: Flank berths for civilian and private ships
precincts.intro: 11,743 × 4,341 ft (3.58 × 1.32 km). Flank berths for civilian and private ships (04 §7.3). Medium berths M1–M15 along the straight hull; a 25-bay skiff marina steps along the hull where it tapers forward of F36.

buildings.name: Harbourmaster
buildings.structure: Concrete frame on an 8 m grid for the horseshoe; a slipformed concrete tower core with a steel and glass cab.
buildings.look: A four-storey horseshoe of pale stone-coloured panels and tall windows, open toward the docks, with a slim 154 ft (47 m) harbour tower standing in front; the tower cab is ringed with green and red navigation lights.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance from the dockside forecourt; staff entrance from the parking on the Dock Road side.
buildings.capacity: About 450 staff; the control cab holds 10 berth controllers.
buildings.services: 4 stair and lift cores plus the tower core; berth radar and comms; backup power.
buildings.interior: A horseshoe of three wings round a harbour garden. Front wing: entrance hall, berth booking counters, pilot assignment and customs liaison on the ground floor, the berth control room on level 2, offices above. Side wings: dock operations, records, pilots' ready room and mess. The tower has radar and comms floors and the harbour control cab at the top.
buildings.purpose: The control office for the bow docks. Harbourmaster staff assign berths, guide ships in and out, and keep the docks running safely.

buildings.name: Bow Docks Fire Station
buildings.structure: Steel portal frame over the appliance hall, 9 m (30 ft) clear; three-storey concrete crew wing.
buildings.look: An L of red-framed glass bay doors along the dock with a taller graphite crew wing turning inland; a lattice drill tower stands in the yard.
buildings.entrances: Six appliance doors onto the dockside apron; crew door from the drill yard.
buildings.capacity: 6 appliances; 20 crew on watch.
buildings.services: Foam refill at every bay, dive and water-rescue store, 2 stair cores with fire poles.
buildings.interior: A six-bay appliance hall facing the dock, and a crew wing with watch room, breathing apparatus, foam store and dive store on the ground floor, bunk rooms, mess and gym above, offices and training on top. Drill tower and yard behind.
buildings.purpose: The fire and rescue station for the bow docks, ready for ship fires, fuel spills and accidents at the berths.

buildings.name: Bow Docks Chandlery
buildings.structure: Steel frame on a 12 m grid with a timber mezzanine; racked steel warehouse behind.
buildings.look: A tall trade hall with a saw-tooth roof of north lights and a glazed front full of goods on display, in weathered bronze and dark metal; the warehouse behind is plain ribbed steel.
buildings.entrances: Trade entrance from the dockside; goods in and out through the loading yard on the stern side.
buildings.capacity: About 2,000 customers a day; 150 staff.
buildings.services: Chilled store for provisions, delivery carts to every berth, 2 stair cores.
buildings.interior: A trade hall with counters for ship parts, rations and provisions, crew outfitting, tools and hardware and navigation charts along a central trade aisle, with account desks and the order office on the mezzanine; a three-part warehouse behind.
buildings.purpose: A ship supply store where crews of docked ships buy spare parts, tools and supplies.

buildings.name: Bow Docks Police Post
buildings.structure: Reinforced concrete frame with hardened ground-floor walls.
buildings.look: A two-storey T in dark basalt panels with a long ribbon window over the dock and a blue light band at the entrance.
buildings.entrances: Public entrance facing the dock; secure vehicle gate on the stern side.
buildings.capacity: About 140 officers across three shifts.
buildings.services: 2 stair cores, custody rooms, drone launch pad on the roof.
buildings.interior: Front desk, customs search rooms, interview rooms and detained-crew rooms on the ground floor; dock security control, open office and briefing room above; a rear wing with evidence store, armoury, drone store and garage between a public garden and a secure yard.
buildings.purpose: The security post for the bow docks, patrolling the berths and checking people and goods coming off the ships.

buildings.name: Repair Yard
buildings.notes: dry bays for small ship repairs
buildings.structure: Two steel sheds, 30 m (98 ft) clear, with 100-tonne overhead cranes on rails; a two-storey concrete workshop row.
buildings.look: Two big pitched sheds in rust-red and graphite ribbed steel with giant doors toward the berths and crane rails running out over the open cradles; the workshop row behind has a long line of yellow-lit windows.
buildings.entrances: Ships come in on transporters from the berths through the shed doors; staff enter from the road-side parking.
buildings.capacity: 4 covered dry bays and 3 open cradles; about 700 workers per shift.
buildings.services: Overhead cranes, compressed air, welding gas, power and water at every bay, 3 stair cores.
buildings.interior: Two repair sheds with two dry bays each, open repair cradles beside them, and a workshop row with machine, welding, hull plating, electrical and pipe shops; canteen and planning offices upstairs.
buildings.purpose: A repair yard with covered dry bays and open cradles where small ships are lifted out of their berths for repairs.

buildings.name: Bow Docks Fuel Depot
buildings.structure: Ten welded steel tanks on ring foundations inside a concrete spill wall; blast-rated pump and control houses.
buildings.look: Two rows of tall grey tanks with orange hazard bands, a pipe bridge running out to the berths, and small dark pump and control houses.
buildings.entrances: Bunker lines run out under the Dock Concourse to every berth; truck bay and staff gate on the stern side.
buildings.capacity: 10 tanks of about 12,000 m³: 120,000 m³ (about 32 million US gallons) of ship fuel.
buildings.services: Bunker pumps to every berth, foam deluge, gas detection, fuel lab.
buildings.interior: Two rows of five bunker tanks inside a spill wall, with the pump house, control house and truck bay at the stern end and the bunker manifold along the dock side.
buildings.purpose: The fuel depot that fills the tanks of ships berthed at the bow docks.

buildings.name: Pilot Lounge
buildings.structure: Two-storey cross-laminated timber on a concrete ground floor.
buildings.look: A long, low timber-and-glass lounge with a planted roof and deep overhangs, warmly lit inside; a calm place on the edge of the docks.
buildings.entrances: Entrance from the drop-off on the Dock Road side; garden doors on the dock side.
buildings.capacity: About 140 rest rooms; the lounge seats 300.
buildings.services: 2 stair cores, 24-hour canteen, blackout blinds upstairs.
buildings.interior: Ground floor: pilots' lounge, canteen, briefing rooms, showers, sleep pods, laundry and gym. Upstairs: a long row of rest rooms and a roof lounge.
buildings.purpose: A rest stop for ship pilots and crews at the bow docks, with rooms and a canteen.

buildings.name: Bow Docks Utility Plant
buildings.structure: Concrete plant house with heavy floors; steel cooling towers.
buildings.look: A small plain graphite plant house with two louvred cooling towers that breathe white vapour.
buildings.entrances: Service doors on the Dock Road side.
buildings.capacity: Power, water and cooling for the front berths; about 15 staff per shift.
buildings.services: Four transformers, water pumps, air handling and two cooling towers.
buildings.interior: A plant house with transformer bays, switch room, water pumps and control room below and air handling above; two cooling towers behind.
buildings.purpose: The utility plant for the bow docks, supplying power, water and cooling to the berths and buildings.

buildings.name: Bow Docks Service Shaft
buildings.structure: Concrete shaft walls down to the 60 m (197 ft) service layer; steel head house.
buildings.look: A narrow windowless head house in graphite metal with yellow-striped lift doors.
buildings.entrances: Vehicle queue on the Dock Road side; staff door into the control house.
buildings.capacity: One vehicle lift and one goods lift to the service layer.
buildings.services: Lift machinery and shaft ventilation.
buildings.interior: A control house and a shaft hall with a vehicle lift and a goods lift down to the service layer.
buildings.purpose: The bow docks' shaft down to the service layer, used for vehicles and goods.

buildings.name: Marina Park
buildings.purpose: A small park beside the bow docks where dock workers and visiting crews can take a break outdoors.

buildings.name: Medium Berths
buildings.purpose: Berths for medium-sized civilian and private ships along the bow flank of the port.

buildings.name: Skiff Marina
buildings.purpose: A marina for small skiffs and private craft at the bow docks.

precincts.name: Stern Docks
precincts.role: Flank berths for civilian and private ships; cross-line Flight Control stop
precincts.intro: 15,169 × 4,341 ft (4.62 × 1.32 km). The big berths: corvettes C1–C8 and frigates F1–F5 (frigate berth rights, 04). The Yard Locks let P8's small craft out to space. The cross-line Flight Control stop at F52 is canon.

buildings.name: Cross-Line Stop
buildings.purpose: The cross-line stop at the stern docks, where the line across the deck to Flight Control picks up and drops off passengers.

buildings.name: Stern Docks Private Flights Lounge
buildings.structure: A long-span steel roof on slender columns over a glass-walled pavilion.
buildings.look: A low floating roof of brushed titanium over full-height glass, with a reflecting water garden behind; warm amber light inside and a single gold line along the roof edge.
buildings.entrances: Valet arrival court facing the berths; garden doors at the back.
buildings.capacity: About 250 guests at a time; 80 staff.
buildings.services: Private customs and immigration, valet to every berth, 2 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: A glass gallery runs the length of the pavilion: owners' check-in and private customs at the front, a main lounge, dining room, private suites and spa along it, a roof bar and meeting suites on top, and a water garden behind.
buildings.purpose: A lounge with its own check-in for passengers of private flights berthed at the stern docks.

buildings.name: Stern Docks Fire Station
buildings.structure: Steel portal frame appliance hall, 9 m (30 ft) clear; a five-storey concrete crew tower.
buildings.look: A long glass-doored appliance hall on the Dock Road, red-framed, with a slim five-storey crew tower at its bow end; a burnt-black training rig shaped like a corvette stands in the yard.
buildings.entrances: Eight appliance doors onto the Dock Road apron; training ground gate on the dock side.
buildings.capacity: 8 appliances; 30 crew on watch; the fire academy trains 120 a day.
buildings.services: Foam and water refill at every bay, 1 stair and lift core, hot-fire training rig.
buildings.interior: An eight-bay appliance hall on the road, a crew tower with watch room and breathing apparatus at ground level, bunk rooms and mess above and fire academy classrooms on top, and a training ground with a mock-corvette fire rig.
buildings.purpose: The main fire and rescue station for the stern docks, which also trains new port firefighters.

buildings.name: Stern Docks Police Post
buildings.structure: Concrete frame with hardened ground floor; steel launch and drone shed.
buildings.look: A three-storey block in charcoal panels with a deep-set ribbon window on every floor and a blue light band; the launch shed beside it has a big blue-striped door.
buildings.entrances: Public entrance facing the berths; patrol launches and drones leave from the shed toward the berths.
buildings.capacity: About 200 officers across three shifts; 2 patrol launches, 12 drones.
buildings.services: 2 stair cores, custody rooms, drone launch pad.
buildings.interior: Front desk, customs search, interview and holding rooms on the ground floor; marine unit room, open office and briefing room on level 2; port security control and intelligence office on top; a shed for patrol launches and drones beside it.
buildings.purpose: The security post for the stern docks, with patrol teams covering the corvette and frigate berths.

buildings.name: Stern Docks Chandlery
buildings.structure: Steel frame bonded store with secure walls; two-storey steel and timber trade building.
buildings.look: A long trade building with a deep timber canopy facing the road and, behind it, a windowless bonded store in dark blue-grey metal with a single row of red security lights.
buildings.entrances: Trade entrance from the road forecourt; goods move between the bonded store and the berths through the loading yard.
buildings.capacity: About 1,500 customers a day; 180 staff.
buildings.services: Customs bond, chilled store, secure parts vault, 2 stair cores.
buildings.interior: A trade building on the road with trade, frigate supply, outfitting and provisions counters and contract and bond offices upstairs; a four-part bonded store behind, including a secure vault for controlled parts.
buildings.purpose: A ship supply store at the stern docks selling parts and supplies to the crews of docked ships.

buildings.name: Corvette Service
buildings.structure: Steel shed, 32 m (105 ft) clear, with twin overhead cranes; concrete workshop wings.
buildings.look: A broad shed in navy-grey ribbed steel with one huge sliding door toward the berths, crowned with a strip of white light; secure systems shop on the stern side with no windows at all.
buildings.entrances: Corvettes come in from the berths through the shed door; staff from the service yard.
buildings.capacity: 2 corvettes under cover; about 500 workers per shift.
buildings.services: Twin 80-tonne cranes, secure armament shop, power and air at both bays, 4 stair cores.
buildings.interior: A two-bay corvette shed opening to the berths, a secure weapons and systems shop on its stern side, and a workshop row with engine, hull and electrical shops, canteen and planning offices.
buildings.purpose: A covered yard where corvettes are repaired and refitted.

buildings.name: Stern Docks Fuel Depot
buildings.structure: Nine welded steel tanks on ring foundations in a concrete spill wall; blast-rated pump and control house.
buildings.look: A square grid of nine tall tanks banded in grey and orange, linked by silver pipe bridges to the berths; a small dark pump house with red safety lights.
buildings.entrances: Bunker lines run under the Berth Road to the corvette and frigate berths; truck bay on the stern side.
buildings.capacity: 9 tanks of about 15,000 m³: 135,000 m³ (about 36 million US gallons) of ship fuel.
buildings.services: Bunker pumps to every berth, foam deluge, gas detection, fuel lab.
buildings.interior: A three-by-three grid of bunker tanks inside a spill wall, with the pump and control house and truck bay on the stern side.
buildings.purpose: The fuel depot that refuels ships berthed at the stern docks.

buildings.name: Frigate Service Yard
buildings.structure: One clear-span steel shed, 42 m (138 ft) high and 300 m (984 ft) deep, with two 200-tonne gantry cranes running out over the crane yard.
buildings.look: The biggest shed in the docks: a tall pitched hall in dark steel with a door the full width of a frigate, and two yellow gantry cranes striding over the open crane yard beside it.
buildings.entrances: Frigates come in on cradles from the berths through the shed door; staff enter from the road-side parking.
buildings.capacity: 1 frigate under cover and 1 in the crane yard; about 1,200 workers per shift.
buildings.services: Two 200-tonne gantry cranes, heavy power and coolant, 3 stair cores.
buildings.interior: A single frigate dock under one great shed, an open crane yard beside it, and a heavy-shops row with engine overhaul, hull plate, armour and shield, and pipe and power shops, with canteen, drawing office and training rooms above.
buildings.purpose: A heavy repair yard with cranes where frigates are worked on, one under cover and one in the open yard.

buildings.name: Company Berth Offices
buildings.structure: Concrete podium with three steel-framed office towers stepping down from 10 to 6 storeys.
buildings.look: Three slim towers of dark mirrored glass rising in steps (10, 8 and 6 storeys) from a stone-clad podium, each with a company crest lit in gold at the top; the plaza in front faces the Dock Road.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance from the company plaza on the Dock Road side; arcade entrances at both ends.
buildings.capacity: About 2,400 office staff for about 40 shipping companies.
buildings.services: 9 stair and lift cores, shared conference centre, members' club.
buildings.interior: A two-storey podium with a central arcade: shared reception, berth leasing hall, bank, insurers and brokers, restaurants and shops, and a conference centre, members' club and gym upstairs. Three office towers above for the shipping companies that lease the frigate berths.
buildings.purpose: Offices for the shipping companies that lease berths at the stern docks, where berth rights and contracts are handled.

buildings.name: Stern Harbourmaster
buildings.structure: Concrete frame on an 8 m grid; a slipformed concrete tower with a steel and glass cab.
buildings.look: A long, low three-storey building of pale stone and dark glass running along the docks, ending in a 167 ft (51 m) tower at the stern end with a ringed glass cab; it mirrors the Bow Docks harbourmaster from the other end of the port.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance from the dockside promenade; staff entrance from the parking.
buildings.capacity: About 600 staff; the control cab holds 12 berth and lock controllers.
buildings.services: 5 stair and lift cores plus the tower core; berth radar and comms; backup power.
buildings.interior: A long building along the docks with entrance hall, booking counters, frigate berth office and pilot assignment on the ground floor, the berth control room, traffic planning and Yard Locks control on level 2, and offices on top; a pilots' wing with ready room, mess and rest rooms; the stern tower with radar floors and the control cab.
buildings.purpose: The control office for the stern docks, assigning berths and guiding ships in and out.

buildings.name: Dock Park
buildings.purpose: A park beside the stern docks for dock workers and visiting crews.

buildings.name: Stern Docks Utility Plant
buildings.structure: Concrete plant floors with blast walls between transformers; steel roof over the plant hall.
buildings.look: Plain graphite sheds with tall louvres and a single long water tank, lit only by small amber lights.
buildings.entrances: Service doors on the dock side.
buildings.capacity: Power, cooling and water for the Stern Docks; about 30 staff per shift.
buildings.services: Six transformers, battery backup, chillers, air handling and water pumps.
buildings.interior: A substation with six transformer bays, a three-bay plant hall for chillers, air handling and water pumps, and a water tank behind.
buildings.purpose: The utility plant for the stern docks, supplying power, cooling and water to the berths and yards.

buildings.name: Stern Docks Service Shaft
buildings.structure: Concrete shaft walls down to the 60 m (197 ft) service layer; steel head house with crane rails.
buildings.look: A tall windowless head house in graphite metal with big louvres and yellow-striped lift doors.
buildings.entrances: Vehicle ramp on the starboard side; staff door into the control house.
buildings.capacity: Two vehicle lifts (one for heavy loads) and one goods lift.
buildings.services: Lift machinery, shaft ventilation, emergency stair.
buildings.interior: A control house with shaft control and fans, and a shaft hall with a heavy vehicle lift, a goods lift and a vehicle lift down to the service layer.
buildings.purpose: The stern docks' shaft to the service layer, with one lift strong enough for heavy loads.

buildings.name: Stern Docks Crew Rest
buildings.structure: Cross-laminated timber on a concrete ground floor, six storeys.
buildings.look: A six-storey ring of rest rooms in pale timber and copper-coloured metal around one big quiet garden, with lit window boxes facing inward.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance from the road forecourt; garden doors from the canteen and lounge.
buildings.capacity: About 2,200 beds in two-bed rest rooms for corvette and frigate crews.
buildings.services: 6 stair and lift cores, blackout shutters, staffed reception around the clock.
buildings.interior: A ring of four wings round a courtyard garden. Ground floor: reception, canteen, lounge, gym, laundry and kitchen in the long wings and rest rooms in the short ones; rest rooms on every floor above.
buildings.purpose: Rest rooms, a canteen and lockers for corvette and frigate crews while their ships are berthed.

buildings.name: Corvette Berths
buildings.purpose: Berths for corvettes along the stern flank of the port.

buildings.name: Frigate Berths
buildings.purpose: Berths for frigates, the largest civilian ships the stern docks take.

buildings.name: Yard Locks
buildings.purpose: Locks where ships pass between the berths and the repair yards.

buildings.name: Yard Taxiway
buildings.purpose: The taxiway that ships use to move between the berths and the yards.

precincts.name: Freight
precincts.intro: 8,463 × 15,584 ft (2.58 × 4.75 km). Cargo and baggage for the whole port, the district's waste, water and air plant, and a freight siding on the Keelway.

buildings.name: Bonded Warehouse A
buildings.structure: Steel portal frames, 18 m (59 ft) clear, on a 30 m grid; customs block in concrete.
buildings.look: A very long sealed shed in blue-grey ribbed steel with customs seals painted at every dock door and a lit band of numbers along the stern side.
buildings.entrances: Forty truck docks along the F35 Street side; customs inspection block at the port end.
buildings.capacity: About 60,000 pallets held in bond; about 200 staff per shift.
buildings.services: Rack sprinklers, customs seals and CCTV on every bay, 2 stair cores.
buildings.interior: A customs inspection block with inspection hall, X-ray tunnel, sample lab and seized goods store, then a 900 m bonded shed split into six halls with docks all along the street side.
buildings.purpose: A secure warehouse where imported goods are stored in bond until customs clears them.

buildings.name: Bonded Warehouse B
buildings.structure: Post-tensioned concrete two-deck warehouse; trucks drive up a ramp to the upper deck.
buildings.look: A two-storey concrete warehouse with long horizontal bands of louvres and a sweeping truck ramp on the stern side; numbered bay doors on both decks.
buildings.entrances: Trucks enter both decks from the truck aisle (upper deck by the ramp); customs and tenant office at the starboard end.
buildings.capacity: 36 bonded bays on two decks for different importers; about 150 staff.
buildings.services: 3 stair and goods-lift cores, sprinklers, customs CCTV.
buildings.interior: Two decks of bonded bays either side of a 24 m truck aisle, reached by a truck ramp, with a customs and tenant office at the end.
buildings.purpose: A second bonded warehouse split into many bays, rented to different importers to store their goods until they are cleared.

buildings.name: Cargo Sorting Hub
buildings.structure: Steel frame on a 24 m grid, 20 m (66 ft) clear, with conveyor mezzanines hung from the roof trusses.
buildings.look: A huge square hall in white and grey panels, ringed by dock doors on both long sides, with a glass control room at the top of the office block looking down into the sorting floor.
buildings.entrances: Inbound trucks dock on the bow side, outbound on the stern side; drivers and staff enter the office block.
buildings.capacity: About 30,000 parcels and 2,000 pallets an hour; about 800 staff per shift.
buildings.services: High-speed sorting conveyors on two levels, 3 stair and lift cores, dock levellers on every door.
buildings.interior: One great sorting hall: inbound unloading, three sorting floors with conveyors overhead and outbound loading, with dock aprons on both sides and an office block with driver reception, customs, canteen, hub control room and planning.
buildings.purpose: The hub where all incoming and outgoing freight is sorted and sent on to its destination.

buildings.name: Baggage Logistics
buildings.notes: all passenger luggage · links P2 and P5
buildings.structure: Steel frame on a 24 m grid with heavy conveyor supports; automated store in a rack-clad steel frame.
buildings.look: A long low hall of graphite panels with a lit strip showing the sorter loops inside, a taller windowless block for the early bag store, and tunnel mouths at the starboard end.
buildings.entrances: Baggage arrives and leaves by tunnels to the Hall of Arrivals and the terminals; staff enter from the bow side.
buildings.capacity: About 18,000 bags an hour; the early bag store holds 40,000 bags.
buildings.services: Four sorter loops, bag screening, automated store, 3 stair cores.
buildings.interior: A staff and control block, a sorter hall with four sorter loops, a screening hall and transfer bags, an automated early bag store, a hall for baggage tugs and carts, and tunnel portals to P2 and P5.
buildings.purpose: The baggage system behind the terminals. It moves, sorts and stores every passenger's luggage between the shuttles, Arrivals and the Terminals.

buildings.name: Freight Fire Station
buildings.structure: Steel appliance hall, 9 m (30 ft) clear; concrete crew and hazmat wings round a courtyard.
buildings.look: A square station of red-trimmed graphite wings around a drill courtyard, with yellow hazmat markings on the decontamination wing.
buildings.entrances: Six appliance doors onto the street apron; crew door from the courtyard.
buildings.capacity: 6 appliances; 22 crew on watch, trained for chemical and fuel spills.
buildings.services: Decontamination suite, chemical lab, 2 stair cores.
buildings.interior: A six-bay appliance hall at the front, a hazmat wing with suit store, decontamination suite and chemical lab on one side, a crew wing with bunk rooms, mess and offices on the other, and a drill courtyard between.
buildings.purpose: The fire station for the freight precinct, with crews trained to deal with chemical and hazardous cargo fires.

buildings.name: Tug Park
buildings.structure: Steel portal frames, 10 m (33 ft) clear, with charging gantries.
buildings.look: A low gunmetal hangar with six tall roller doors striped yellow and black, and a yard of haulers under floodlights.
buildings.entrances: Bay doors to the freight roads; crew entrance at the side.
buildings.capacity: About 60 tugs and 40 haulers.
buildings.services: Charging in every bay, tug workshop, 2 stair cores.
buildings.interior: A six-bay hangar for tugs and haulers with a tug workshop, a crew and control strip with dispatch, drivers' room and fleet control, and a hauler parking yard.
buildings.purpose: The yard where tugs and haulers are parked between jobs moving cargo around the port.

buildings.name: Cold Store
buildings.structure: Insulated sandwich-panel chambers inside a steel frame, with heated floors to stop frost heave.
buildings.look: A white, almost windowless block with a frosted blue light line along the top, and a long chilled dock with sealed doors on the starboard side.
buildings.entrances: Eight sealed chilled docks on the starboard side; staff enter through the plant block.
buildings.capacity: About 35,000 pallets frozen and 15,000 chilled, including the port's medical cold vault.
buildings.services: Ammonia-free refrigeration plant, backup power for the medical vault, 2 stair cores.
buildings.interior: Three deep-freeze chambers and four chill rooms (chill, fresh produce, medical vault, ripening), a sealed chilled dock hall with quality inspection, and the refrigeration plant behind.
buildings.purpose: A refrigerated warehouse for food and medical supplies that must be kept frozen or chilled.

buildings.name: Warehouse C
buildings.structure: Steel portal frames, 12 m (39 ft) clear, with fire walls between the six units.
buildings.look: Six warehouse units under one long roof in alternating light and dark grey bands, each with its own lit unit number and office front.
buildings.entrances: Each unit has its own office entrance at the front and docks on the yard side.
buildings.capacity: 6 rentable units, about 7,600 m² each; about 300 staff in all.
buildings.services: Fire walls between units, 3 stair cores in the office strip.
buildings.interior: Six rentable warehouse units side by side, each with its own reception and offices at the front and docks onto a shared yard.
buildings.purpose: A general warehouse split into units rented by businesses that need storage near the port.

buildings.name: Waste Transfer & Recycling
buildings.structure: Concrete push-walls in the tipping hall, steel frame elsewhere, sealed and kept under negative air pressure.
buildings.look: A long green-grey shed with two round digester tanks and a short exhaust stack; trucks run down a lane along its stern side.
buildings.entrances: Collection trucks enter from the truck lanes and the weighbridge; staff through the office.
buildings.capacity: About 900 tonnes of the district's waste a day.
buildings.services: Odour control, two organics digesters making gas for the utility plant.
buildings.interior: A tipping hall, a recovery hall with sorting line and stores for metals, glass, plastics and paper, two organics digesters, a bale store and a weighbridge office.
buildings.purpose: Where the district's waste is collected, sorted and recycled before being sent on.

buildings.name: Freight Utility Plant
buildings.structure: Concrete plant floors with blast walls; steel roof.
buildings.look: Plain graphite sheds with tall louvres and two water tanks, lit by small amber lights.
buildings.entrances: Service doors on the F35 Street side.
buildings.capacity: Power, cooling and heat for P4; about 30 staff per shift.
buildings.services: Eight transformers, chillers, air handling, heat from the waste digesters.
buildings.interior: A substation with eight transformer bays, a plant hall with chillers, air handling and boilers, and two water tanks.
buildings.purpose: The utility plant for the freight precinct, supplying power, cooling and heat.

buildings.name: Freight Service Shaft
buildings.structure: Concrete shaft walls down to the 60 m (197 ft) service layer; steel head house with crane rails.
buildings.look: A tall graphite head house with heavy louvres and yellow-striped lift doors big enough for containers.
buildings.entrances: Truck queue on the starboard side; staff door into the control house.
buildings.capacity: A heavy freight lift, a container lift and a vehicle lift.
buildings.services: Lift machinery, shaft ventilation, emergency stair.
buildings.interior: A control house and a shaft hall with a heavy freight lift, a container lift and a vehicle lift down to the service layer, with a truck queue behind.
buildings.purpose: The freight precinct's shaft to the service layer, with lifts big enough for containers and heavy freight.

buildings.name: Service Plant
buildings.structure: Heavy concrete plant halls, 24 m (79 ft) high, over a 12 m deep pump level.
buildings.look: Four tall plant halls with giant louvred walls that breathe air for the service layer below, beside a lower water treatment hall; the whole block is graphite with slow-pulsing white light bands.
buildings.entrances: Service yard on the starboard side; staff through the control building.
buildings.capacity: Air and water for the Port of Arrivals service layer; about 120 staff per shift.
buildings.services: Air handling for the service layer, water filtration and treatment, deep pumps, 2 stair cores.
buildings.interior: Four air handling halls, a water treatment line (filtration, treatment tanks and clean water reservoir), a deep water pump station and a control building with the plant control room, water lab and workshop.
buildings.purpose: A plant that pumps water and handles air for the service layer under the whole Port of Arrivals.

buildings.name: Ground Vehicle Depot
buildings.structure: Steel truck hall, 8 m (26 ft) clear; concrete pod decks above the ground deck.
buildings.look: A low truck hall and a four-deck pod garage side by side, wrapped in perforated gunmetal screens with green charging lights showing through.
buildings.entrances: Vehicles in and out from both cross streets; drivers through the dispatch block.
buildings.capacity: About 400 trucks and 3,000 pods.
