buildings.services: Charging at every space, vehicle wash, 2 stair cores.
buildings.interior: A truck hall with four parking and charging bays, four pod decks beside it, a dispatch block with drivers' room, canteen and fleet control, and a wash and charge yard.
buildings.purpose: The depot for the port's own vehicles: trucks, ground pods and service vehicles are parked and dispatched from here.

buildings.name: Forwarders
buildings.structure: Steel frame with timber-concrete floors on a 7.5 m grid.
buildings.look: A small campus of four office blocks in brick-red metal and glass around a shared garden, each with a forwarder's sign lit on its gable.
buildings.entrances: Each block has its own entrance from the garden; parking on the Freight Road side.
buildings.capacity: About 1,500 staff for about 60 freight forwarders and brokers.
buildings.services: 9 stair and lift cores, shared conference rooms, canteen and gym.
buildings.interior: Three office blocks along the front and a long back block round a shared garden: shared reception, customs broker desks, freight booking hall, bank, insurance and courier counters on the ground floors, forwarder offices above.
buildings.purpose: Offices for freight forwarding firms that book and arrange cargo shipments through the port.

buildings.name: Vehicle Workshop
buildings.structure: Steel portal frames, 12 m (39 ft) clear, with service pits and a 20-tonne crane in the heavy hall.
buildings.look: A wide gunmetal workshop with a row of roller doors, each numbered and lit, and a red-painted heavy truck hall at the stern end.
buildings.entrances: Roller doors onto the vehicle yard; staff through the shops strip.
buildings.capacity: 13 bays; about 250 mechanics per shift.
buildings.services: Service pits, vehicle lifts, 20-tonne crane, 2 stair cores.
buildings.interior: A service hall with ten pit bays, a heavy truck hall with three bays, and a shops strip with tyre, battery, paint and body shops and parts store; canteen and offices above.
buildings.purpose: A workshop where the port's trucks, pods and service vehicles are maintained and repaired.

buildings.name: Container Yard
buildings.structure: Heavy concrete pavement for container stacks five high; two rail-mounted gantry cranes, 25 m (82 ft) tall, over the Keelway siding.
buildings.look: Rows of containers stacked five high in every colour, with two tall yellow gantry cranes straddling the Keelway siding at the starboard end; a small glass gate house at the front.
buildings.entrances: Trucks through the gate house lanes on the port side; freight trains on the Keelway siding at the starboard side.
buildings.capacity: About 6,000 containers (one row plugged in for refrigerated boxes).
buildings.services: Reefer power points, crane power rails, floodlights, customs scanning at the gate.
buildings.interior: A gate house with gate control and customs check, four container stack rows and a refrigerated row, and a crane runway where two gantry cranes load the Keelway freight trains.
buildings.purpose: A container yard beside the Keelway freight siding, where containers are stacked and loaded on and off trains.

precincts.name: Shuttle Yards
precincts.role: Public small-craft hangars, shuttle depot, maintenance, fuel
precincts.intro: 11,888 × 15,584 ft (3.62 × 4.75 km). Public hangars for everyone's small craft and the shuttle depot. Craft taxi north along the Yard Taxiway to the Yard Locks in P3. The Atrium Plaza (canon) is not part of the precinct.

buildings.name: Maintenance Shops
buildings.structure: Four steel barrel-vault halls, 24 m (79 ft) clear inside, each spanning 260 m (853 ft) with no columns; a two-storey concrete workshop spine behind them.
buildings.look: Four barrel-vaulted halls in ribbed gunmetal steel, each with a 300 m glazed folding door facing the taxiway that glows amber at night; behind them a low dark workshop spine with a continuous strip of high windows.
buildings.entrances: One 300 m folding hangar door per hall onto the apron; staff entrance in the middle of the workshop spine, off the pod park.
buildings.capacity: 4 halls, 8 craft bays; about 900 technicians per shift.
buildings.services: Overhead cranes in every hall, compressed air and power at each bay, foam fire suppression, 3 stair and lift cores in the spine.
buildings.interior: Four halls side by side, each split into two craft bays. Behind them the workshop spine: engine, avionics, composites and wheel shops, test lab, tool cribs and parts cage on the ground floor; planning office, records, training rooms and canteen upstairs, all opening onto a 6 m workshop street.
buildings.purpose: Workshops where shuttles and small craft have their engines, avionics and safety inspections done.

buildings.name: Shuttle Ops
buildings.structure: Concrete frame on a 9 m grid for the courtyard ring; a slipformed concrete tower core with a steel-framed glass control cab on top.
buildings.look: A three-storey ring of smoked glass and brushed titanium around a planted courtyard, with a slim 42 m (138 ft) tower rising on the airside edge; the tower ends in a faceted glass cab that is lit blue-white so pilots can find it from anywhere in the yards.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance from the forecourt on the port side; crew gate straight onto the airside apron beside the tower.
buildings.capacity: About 600 staff across three shifts; the control cab holds 12 controllers.
buildings.services: 6 stair and lift cores plus the tower core; backup power and comms room; the courtyard is the fire assembly point.
buildings.interior: Four wings round a garden courtyard. Ground floor: lobby and café on the entrance side, crew check-in and lounge on the bow side, weather and flight planning on the stern side, briefing rooms and the crew gate on the airside. Upstairs: the dispatch floor, scheduling, training and offices. The tower holds planning floors and the yard control cab at the top.
buildings.purpose: The operations centre for the shuttle service, setting schedules and dispatching shuttles.

buildings.name: Fuel Farm
buildings.structure: Twelve welded steel tanks on concrete ring foundations inside a 2 m (6.6 ft) concrete spill wall; pump and control houses in blast-rated concrete.
buildings.look: Twelve squat white-banded steel tanks in a neat grid behind a low concrete wall, with a pipe rack running out to the apron; small graphite pump and control houses with red safety lighting.
buildings.entrances: Fuel truck gate and loading gantry on the stern side; staff door into the control house; hydrant lines run under the apron to every stand.
buildings.capacity: 12 tanks of about 8,000 m³ each: 96,000 m³ (about 25 million US gallons) of shuttle fuel.
buildings.services: Hydrant pumps to the apron, foam deluge over every tank, gas detection, a fuel quality lab.
buildings.interior: Tank grid inside the spill wall, with the pump house, control and foam house and truck gantry along the stern side and the hydrant valve pits along the apron edge.
buildings.purpose: The fuel depot for the shuttle yards, refuelling shuttles and small craft.

buildings.name: Owner Hangars
buildings.structure: Eight rows of steel-framed hangar bays, 30 × 40 m (98 × 131 ft) each, built back to back in pairs; a two-storey timber-and-steel clubhouse.
buildings.look: Long low rows of gunmetal hangars with numbered roller doors, each lit by its own white door light; the clubhouse is warm timber and glass with a deep roof terrace looking over the taxilanes.
buildings.entrances: Every bay has its own roller door onto a taxilane; the taxilanes open onto the Yard Taxiway at the port end. Clubhouse entrance from the visitor parking.
buildings.capacity: 256 leased bays (one small craft each), in 8 rows of 32.
buildings.services: Power, air and fuel point in every bay, sprinklers in every row, CCTV and owner key access.
buildings.interior: Four pairs of hangar rows with a taxilane between each pair, running from the taxiway to the back of the lot. The clubhouse on the stern side has the lounge, leasing office, pilot shop, café and flight planning on the ground floor and members' rooms and a function room upstairs.
buildings.purpose: Rows of hangar bays leased to private owners who keep their small craft aboard.

buildings.name: Shuttle Yards Fire Station
buildings.structure: Steel portal frame over a drive-through appliance hall, 9 m (30 ft) clear; concrete frame for the three-storey crew block and the watch tower.
buildings.look: A long low hall of glass bay doors framed in red-trimmed graphite panels, with a slim 18 m (59 ft) watch tower at one end lit red at the top; the crew block above has deep-set windows.
buildings.entrances: Eight glass appliance doors straight onto the airside forecourt and the taxiway; crew door and road-side exit on the starboard side.
buildings.capacity: 8 crash tenders; 24 crew on watch.
buildings.services: Foam and water refill points in every bay, exhaust extraction, 2 stair cores with fire poles, standby generator.
buildings.interior: A drive-through appliance hall with 8 bays facing the taxiway. Behind it the crew block: watch room, breathing apparatus and decontamination on the ground floor, bunk rooms, kitchen, mess and gym on level 2, offices and training on level 3. Drill yard and a mock-craft training rig behind.
buildings.purpose: The fire and rescue station for the shuttle yards, with crash tenders ready for craft accidents.

buildings.name: Shuttle Yards Police Post
buildings.structure: Reinforced concrete frame on an 8 m grid with hardened ground-floor walls.
buildings.look: A compact two-storey block of dark basalt-grey panels with narrow vertical windows and a lit blue band over the glass entrance.
buildings.entrances: Public entrance from the small plaza on the stern side; secure vehicle gate at the back.
buildings.capacity: About 120 officers across three shifts.
buildings.services: 2 stair cores, secure custody suite, backup power, CCTV link to the yard control cab.
buildings.interior: Front desk, interview rooms, custody and holding cells on the ground floor; open office, control and briefing rooms upstairs; a garage wing with evidence store and armoury around a secure yard.
buildings.purpose: The security post for the shuttle yards, guarding the hangars and checking who comes and goes.

buildings.name: Parts & Avionics
buildings.structure: A 20 m (66 ft) steel high-bay store with robot rack aisles; a three-storey concrete lab wing with vibration-isolated floors.
buildings.look: A tall, almost windowless box in silver-grey ribbed metal with a band of white light around the top; beside it a glass-fronted lab wing showing the benches inside.
buildings.entrances: Airside dispatch doors straight to the apron; truck docks on the starboard side; trade counter entrance on the stern side.
buildings.capacity: About 300,000 stored parts in 5 robot aisles; about 350 staff.
buildings.services: Robot rack system, clean-room air, static-safe floors, 3 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: An automated high-bay parts store with five robot aisles, airside dispatch on one side and truck docks on the other. The lab wing holds avionics test benches, a clean room, antenna and calibration labs and repair floors; the trade counter, goods-in inspection and purchasing sit beside it.
buildings.purpose: A store for craft spare parts and avionics, kept in robot-served aisles for the yard's workshops.

buildings.name: Paint & Refit
buildings.structure: Sealed steel-framed halls, 22 m (72 ft) clear, with pressurised air and fire-rated walls; a two-storey concrete support block.
buildings.look: Two smooth white sealed paint halls and a darker refit hangar side by side, their doors striped with colour test panels; filter stacks and the air treatment plant behind.
buildings.entrances: Hall doors face the apron and the taxiway; staff and goods enter the support block from the service yard.
buildings.capacity: 2 paint halls and 2 refit bays (4 craft at once); about 250 staff.
buildings.services: Down-draft paint booths with filtered exhaust, heated curing, solvent recovery, 2 stair cores.
buildings.interior: Two sealed paint halls and a two-bay refit hangar along the apron, four sanding and masking bays behind the paint halls, and a support block with paint mixing, solvent store, upholstery and interiors shop, livery design studio and canteen.
buildings.purpose: Halls where small craft are repainted and refitted.

buildings.name: Yard Offices
buildings.structure: Steel frame with timber-concrete composite floors on a 7.5 m grid.
buildings.look: An L-shaped five-storey office with full-height smart glass behind slim bronze-coloured fins, wrapped around a sunken garden; the top floor steps back for a roof terrace.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance from the plaza facing the Yard Road; garden doors on the courtyard side.
buildings.capacity: About 900 staff.
buildings.services: 3 stair and lift cores, raised floors, solar-tinting glass, rainwater for the garden.
buildings.interior: An L of two office wings round a garden. Ground floor: entrance hall, customs and permits desk, leasing and berth rights office, bank and insurance desk, café, conference hall and training rooms. Upper floors: open offices, meeting rooms, private offices, yard management and records.
buildings.purpose: Offices for the staff who run the shuttle yards.

buildings.name: Shuttle Yards Utility Plant
buildings.structure: Heavy concrete plant floors and blast walls between transformer bays; steel roof over the chiller hall.
buildings.look: Plain graphite metal sheds with louvred walls and two round-topped water tanks, lit only by small amber service lights.
buildings.entrances: Service gate and transformer doors on the stern side; tanker access to the water tanks.
buildings.capacity: Power, cooling and water for all of P8; about 30 staff per shift.
buildings.services: Six transformers, battery backup, chillers and air handlers feeding the yards.
buildings.interior: A substation with six transformer bays, switch, battery and control rooms; a three-bay chiller, air handling and heat exchanger hall; two water tanks at the back.
buildings.purpose: The utility plant for the shuttle yards, supplying power, cooling and water.

buildings.name: Shuttle Yards Service Shaft
buildings.structure: Concrete shaft walls down to the 60 m (197 ft) service layer; steel head house with crane rails over the lifts.
buildings.look: A tall windowless head house in graphite metal with big louvres and yellow-striped lift doors.
buildings.entrances: Vehicle queue and ramp on the starboard side; staff door into the control house.
buildings.capacity: Two vehicle lifts and one goods lift to the service layer.
buildings.services: Lift machinery, shaft ventilation fans, emergency stair down the shaft.
buildings.interior: Control house with shaft control and fans; the shaft hall holds two vehicle lifts and a goods lift that run down to the service layer; vehicles queue on the ramp behind.
buildings.purpose: The shuttle yards' shaft to the service layer for vehicles and goods.

buildings.name: Shuttle Yards Crew Rest
buildings.structure: Cross-laminated timber floors on a concrete ground floor, 3.4 m (11 ft) storeys.
buildings.look: Three timber-clad sleeping wings reaching toward the taxiway with planted gardens between them, joined by a glazed road-side block; deep window reveals and blackout shutters for day sleepers.
buildings.entrances: Main entrance from the Yard Road side; garden doors from the canteen and lounge.
buildings.capacity: About 1,400 beds in two-bed rest rooms for crews between shifts.
buildings.services: 5 stair and lift cores, sound-insulated walls, blackout shutters, staffed reception around the clock.
buildings.interior: A road-side block with reception, canteen, lounge, gym and laundry on the ground floor and rest rooms above; three sleeping wings of single rest rooms on every floor, with gardens between the wings.
buildings.purpose: Rest rooms for yard crews between shifts.

buildings.name: Atrium Edge Park
buildings.purpose: A large park at the edge of the Atrium Plaza, separating the busy shuttle yards from the plaza and giving yard workers green space.

buildings.name: Shuttle Yards Pod Depot
buildings.notes: shortened from 1,500 m on 26 Nov 2026 so it stays clear of the canon Atrium Plaza
buildings.structure: Post-tensioned concrete parking decks with ramps at each end; steel canopy over the wash and service bays.
buildings.look: Open-sided parking decks with perforated gunmetal screens and lines of green charging lights; a small glass dispatch office at the front.
buildings.entrances: Pod lanes in and out at the starboard end; dispatch office faces the Yard Road.
buildings.capacity: About 2,400 ground pods on three decks.
buildings.services: Charging at every space, pod wash, battery swap, 2 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: Three parking and charging decks, a wash and service block with pod wash, battery swap and repair bays, and a dispatch office with booking hall and fleet control.
buildings.purpose: The depot where the yards' ground pods are parked and charged.

buildings.name: Hangar Row A
buildings.structure: Steel portal frame per bay, one full-width door to the apron.
buildings.look: Gunmetal sheds with full-width bay doors and a light strip over each door. Port of Arrivals style: graphite and gunmetal metal cladding, white exterior light lines.
buildings.entrances: One full-width craft door per bay on the apron side; a staff door at the back.
buildings.services: Power, air and fuel points in every bay; fire suppression over each bay.
buildings.interior: Each bay is one open floor for a craft, with a small tool room and a staff door at the back.
buildings.capacity: 31 bays, one craft each
buildings.purpose: A row of public hangar bays for small craft, one craft to a bay.

buildings.name: Shuttle Depot
buildings.structure: Steel portal frame per bay, one full-width door to the apron (same size as the arrival gates).
buildings.look: Gunmetal sheds with full-width bay doors and a light strip over each door. Port of Arrivals style: graphite and gunmetal metal cladding, white exterior light lines.
buildings.entrances: One full-width craft door per bay on the apron side; a staff door at the back.
buildings.services: Power, air and fuel points in every bay; fire suppression over each bay.
buildings.interior: Each bay is one open floor for a craft, with a small tool room and a staff door at the back.
buildings.capacity: 16 bays, one craft each
buildings.purpose: The depot where the port's own passenger shuttles are kept and readied between flights.

buildings.name: Hangar Row B
buildings.structure: Steel portal frame per bay, one full-width door to the apron.
buildings.look: Gunmetal sheds with full-width bay doors and a light strip over each door. Port of Arrivals style: graphite and gunmetal metal cladding, white exterior light lines.
buildings.entrances: One full-width craft door per bay on the apron side; a staff door at the back.
buildings.services: Power, air and fuel points in every bay; fire suppression over each bay.
buildings.interior: Each bay is one open floor for a craft, with a small tool room and a staff door at the back.
buildings.capacity: 62 bays, one craft each
buildings.purpose: A long row of public hangar bays for small craft.

buildings.name: Shuttle Yards Training Centre
buildings.notes: pilot and ground-crew training · simulators · fills an empty block (proposed 27 Nov 2026)
buildings.structure: Steel frame with isolated slabs under the simulators; concrete classroom block.
buildings.look: A crisp white box for the simulators with a glass classroom block in front, its stair towers lit blue; the training hangar behind has a full-glass door so the practice craft can be seen.
buildings.entrances: Entrance from the courtyard; training hangar door to the yard.
buildings.capacity: 8 full-motion simulators; about 400 trainees a day.
buildings.services: Simulator power and cooling, 2 stair and lift cores.
buildings.interior: Eight full-motion flight simulator bays, a classroom block with briefing rooms, classrooms, library and exam hall, a ground-school courtyard and a training hangar with practice craft.
buildings.purpose: A training centre for shuttle pilots and ground crews, with simulators and classrooms.

buildings.name: Engine Test Hall
buildings.notes: engine runs and test cells · fills an empty block (proposed 27 Nov 2026)
buildings.structure: Thick double concrete walls and roofs round each test cell, with acoustic baffles in the air intakes and exhaust stacks.
buildings.look: Three heavy concrete blocks with tall square exhaust stacks, their sides lined with acoustic louvres; a slim glass control block at the end where engineers watch the runs.
buildings.entrances: Engines arrive by the transfer yard; each cell has a heavy rolling door from the yard road.
buildings.capacity: 3 test cells (3 engines at once).
buildings.services: Engine fuel supply, intake and exhaust silencers, fire suppression in each cell, 2 stair cores.
buildings.interior: Three sound-proof engine test cells in a row, then the engine prep shop and stores with three test control rooms, a data room and a viewing gallery above.
buildings.purpose: A hall with test cells where repaired engines are run and checked before going back into a craft.

buildings.name: Yard Stores
buildings.notes: spares and consumables for the yards · fills an empty block (proposed 27 Nov 2026)
buildings.structure: Steel portal frames, 18 m (59 ft) clear, with a flat heavy-duty floor for the racks.
buildings.look: A long ribbed gunmetal store with one band of high windows and a yellow-lit receiving canopy at the end.
buildings.entrances: Receiving dock and issue counter at the starboard end; fire doors along the sides.
buildings.capacity: About 40,000 pallet spaces; about 80 staff per shift.
buildings.services: Rack sprinklers, forklift charging, 1 stair core.
buildings.interior: Six high-bay rack blocks, a bulk store for consumables and heavy spares, and a receiving block with dock, goods-in check, issue counter and stock control.
buildings.purpose: The stores building that keeps the yards supplied with spares and consumables.
